title: Life in St. Mary's; childhood comparison
description: Linda Appel discusses the advantages and disadvantages of living in St. Mary's, noting the recreation opportunities and small community feel versus the lack of shopping, which requires trips to Spokane. She compares her current farm life with her childhood on a farm in Redmond, Oregon, where the landscape was flat sagebrush and juniper.

title: Farm animals; the five children
description: Appel describes the family’s animals, including cows that are summering at her father-in-law's place, a pet horse they sold after the flood, and the children's rabbits and pets. She then details her five children—Cheryl, Ginger, Jackie, Wendy, and the baby boy—and their interests in band, church youth club, sports, and outdoor play.

title: The January flood; the relocated house
description: She recounts how the January flood put five and a half feet of water in their home, destroying belongings and requiring extensive cleanup. The family moved the house 700 feet back from the river onto a new foundation, where it now overlooks the river, Baldy mountain, and the valley lake.

title: Family recreation; husband's logging work
description: Appel describes family recreation such as fishing behind the house and snow catting in the winter, noting that the family does most activities together. She explains that her husband works as a logging contractor for Potlatch, continuing the logging career he has had since their marriage and that he was born and raised in St. Mary's.

title: Community activities; household decisions; town needs
description: She explains that home responsibilities keep her too busy for many clubs, though she joined and later quit MNL, and that she handles most family decisions while her husband is away. She identifies the town's need for better streets, sidewalks, street lighting, and youth facilities like a movie theater, bowling alley, or roller rink so children do not have to bus to Spokane.

title: Little League; girls' exclusion; flood cleanup help
description: The conversation turns to Little League softball and the previous year's controversy when girls were told they could not join the boys' teams after trying out. She also describes how two busloads of university students helped clear debris from their property and scrubbed houses after the flood, work that would have taken the family weeks to complete alone.
